Main.sentence: The ___E:1985 season U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_NFL_season)___ was the ___E:Chicago Bears U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bears)___ ' 66th in the ___E:National Football League U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League)___ (NFL) and their fourth under ___E:head coach U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Chicago_Bears_head_coaches)___ ___E:Mike Ditka U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Ditka)___ .

The Bears entered 1985 looking to improve on their 10–6 record from 1984 and advance further than the ___E:NFC Championship Game U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFC_Championship_Game)___ , where they lost to the 15–1 ___E:San Francisco 49ers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_San_Francisco_49ers_season)___ .
The Bears not only improved on that record, they put together what would be considered by many football historians the greatest season in NFL history.
The Bears won their first twelve games of the season before losing to the ___E:Miami Dolphins U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_Miami_Dolphins_season)___ on Monday Night Football .
The loss to the Dolphins would be the only loss the Bears would suffer that season, as they finished with a 15–1 record.

This matched the 49ers' mark from the year before and tied the then-record for most wins in a regular season; the record would be reached twice more in 1998 ( ___E:Minnesota Vikings U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_Minnesota_Vikings_season)___ ) and 2004 ( ___E:Pittsburgh Steelers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Pittsburgh_Steelers_season)___ ) before the ___E:New England Patriots U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_England_Patriots_season)___ ended the ___E:2007 NFL season U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_NFL_season)___ with a 16–0 regular season record.
The Bears' defense was ranked first in the league and only allowed 198 total points (an average of 12.4 points per game).

The Bears won the NFC Central Division by seven games over the second-place ___E:Green Bay Packers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_Green_Bay_Packers_season)___ and earned home-field advantage throughout the playoffs as the NFC’s top seed at ___E:Soldier Field U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soldier_Field)___ .

In their two playoff games against the ___E:New York Giants U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_New_York_Giants_season)___ and ___E:Los Angeles Rams U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_Los_Angeles_Rams_season)___ , the Bears outscored their opponents 45–0 and became the first team to record back-to-back playoff shutouts.

Then, in ___E:Super Bowl XX U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XX)___ at the ___E:Louisiana Superdome U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz_Superdome)___ against the ___E:New England Patriots U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_New_England_Patriots_season)___ , the Bears set several more records.

First, their 46 points broke the previous record of 38 that had been scored by the ___E:Los Angeles Raiders U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1983_Los_Angeles_Raiders_season)___ in ___E:Super Bowl XVIII U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XVIII)___ and again by the 49ers in ___E:Super Bowl XIX U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XIX)___ .

Their 36-point margin of victory also topped the 29-point margin of victory that the Raiders recorded over the ___E:Washington Redskins U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1983_Washington_Redskins_season)___ in Super Bowl XVIII.

Both of those records would stand until ___E:Super Bowl XXIV U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXIV)___ in New Orleans four years later, when the ___E:49ers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_San_Francisco_49ers_season)___ defeated the ___E:Denver Broncos U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_Denver_Broncos_season)___ by 45 points, 55–10. This was the Bears' first championship since ___E:1963 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1963_NFL_Championship_Game)___ and is their most recent title.

The 1985 Chicago Bears are one of the few teams to consistently challenge the ___E:undefeated 1972 Miami Dolphins U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_Miami_Dolphins_season)___ for the title of the greatest NFL team of all time.   In 2007, the 1985 Bears were ranked as the second greatest Super Bowl championship team on the ___E:NFL Network U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Network)___ 's documentary series America's Game: The Super Bowl Champions , ranking behind only the 1972 Dolphins.
They also ranked #2 behind only the Dolphins on the 100 greatest teams of all time presented by the NFL on its 100th anniversary.
Other sources rate the 1985 Chicago Bears as the greatest NFL team ever.

The defense led the league in points allowed (198), yards allowed (4,135) and takeaways (54), a feat that wasn't accomplished again until the ___E:2013 Seattle Seahawks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Seattle_Seahawks_season)___ ___E:defense U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legion_of_Boom_(Seattle_Seahawks))___ .

After the draft, the Bears signed 3 undrafted free agents, quarterback ___E:Mike Tomczak U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Tomczak)___ from ___E:Ohio State U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_State_Buckeyes_football)___ , along with defensive back ___E:Ken Taylor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Taylor_(American_football))___ and receiver ___E:Keith Ortego U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Ortego)___ of ___E:Oregon State U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oregon_State_Beavers_football)___ and ___E:McNeese State U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McNeese_State_Cowboys_and_Cowgirls)___ , respectively.

In a trade with the ___E:San Diego Chargers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Chargers)___ , the Bears acquired linebacker ___E:Cliff Thrift U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cliff_Thrift)___ and punter ___E:Maury Buford U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maury_Buford)___ by trading away their 12th round draft picks from 1985 and 1986, respectively.

During training camp, seven players, including ___E:Mike Singletary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Singletary)___ , ___E:Steve McMichael U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_McMichael)___ , ___E:Keith Van Horne U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Van_Horne)___ and rookie ___E:William Perry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Perry_(American_football))___ , were either unsigned or holding out due to their contracts.
Perry, McMichael and Van Horne eventually reported to training camp. Perry held out until August 5, when he signed a four-year, $1.35 million contract.
However, after an unimpressive showing at training camp, defensive coordinator ___E:Buddy Ryan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddy_Ryan)___ tabbed Perry as a "wasted draft-pick".

Before the team's season opening game against the ___E:Tampa Bay Buccaneers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa_Bay_Buccaneers)___ , players ___E:Al Harris U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Harris_(defensive_lineman))___ , ___E:Todd Bell U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Todd_Bell)___ and ___E:Richard Dent U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Dent)___ requested to be traded.

Dent and the Bears had been attempting to work out a contract extension, as his contract ran through the 1985 season, and paid him $90,000. Bell played for $77,000 the year before, and made the ___E:1985 Pro Bowl U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_Pro_Bowl)___ roster, but asked for $950,000 annually, which would have made him the highest-paid player on the team. Bell and Harris would eventually hold out for the season.

The Bears had allowed 212 yards in the first half, but eventually allowed only 95 in the second half. ___E:Walter Payton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Payton)___ had rushed for 120 yards on 17 carries, and McMahon completed 23/34 passes for 274 yards, two touchdowns and one interception.

In return for 49ers coach ___E:Bill Walsh U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Walsh_(American_football_coach))___ ’s idea of sending lineman ___E:Guy McIntyre U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guy_McIntyre)___ in as fullback the season before, ___E:Mike Ditka U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Ditka)___ sent in rookie ___E:William Perry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Perry_(American_football))___ , but as a runner rather than a blocker.

The Bears’ hopes for a perfect season were thwarted when ___E:Dan Marino U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Marino)___ and the Dolphins defeated the McMahon-less Bears on ___E:Monday Night Football U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monday_Night_Football)___ , 38–24. The Dolphins' victory persevered their ___E:1972 season U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_Miami_Dolphins)___ as the only undefeated regular season in the NFL since the ___E:AFL–NFL merger U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFL%E2%80%93NFL_merger)___ , a feat that would not be equaled until 2007 when the ___E:2007 New England Patriots U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_England_Patriots)___ went undefeated through the regular season.
Miami struck first when Marino hit ___E:Nat Moore U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nat_Moore)___ for a 33-yard touchdown.

Bears backup ___E:Steve Fuller U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Fuller_(American_football))___ then threw a 69-yard pass to ___E:Willie Gault U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Gault)___ , and eventually snuck in for a 1-yard touchdown.

After a ___E:Fuad Reveiz U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fuad_Reveiz)___ field goal to put Miami up 10–7, Marino hit Moore again that set up a ___E:Ron Davenport U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Davenport)___ touchdown to increase the gap by 10 points.

After the Bears scored on a ___E:Kevin Butler U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Butler_(American_football))___ field goal, Marino hit ___E:Mark Duper U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Duper)___ on a crossing pattern for 52 yards.

Davenport then ran in, and the Dolphins led 24–10. Later, the Dolphins would increase their lead to 31–10. The Bears had not allowed 31 points in one half since the ___E:1972 season opener U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_Chicago_Bears_season)___ .

The Bears then scored in the third quarter, but any momentum they gained was lost when Butler muffed the ensuing kickoff, which Dolphins rookie ___E:Alex Moyer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Moyer)___ recovered at the Bears 46. ___E:Dan Hampton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Hampton)___ then tipped a Marino pass into the air, but it sailed downfield for 30 yards before landing in the hands of Clayton, who went into the end zone to make it 38–17. Fuller hit ___E:Ken Margerum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Margerum)___ for a 19-yard touchdown, but that would be the last score of the night for the Bears.

The Patriots took a quick lead after linebacker ___E:Larry McGrew U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_McGrew)___ recovered a fumble from ___E:Walter Payton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Payton)___ at the Chicago 19-yard line on the second play of the game, setting up ___E:Tony Franklin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Franklin_(placekicker))___ 's 36-yard field goal 1:19 into the first quarter.

The Bears struck back with a 7-play, 59-yard drive, featuring a 43-yard pass completion from ___E:Jim McMahon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_McMahon)___ to wide receiver ___E:Willie Gault U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Gault)___ , to set up a field goal from ___E:Kevin Butler U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Butler_(American_football))___ , tying the score 3–3.

After both teams traded punts, ___E:Richard Dent U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Dent)___ and linebacker ___E:Wilber Marshall U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilber_Marshall)___ shared a sack on Eason, forcing a fumble that lineman ___E:Dan Hampton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Hampton)___ recovered on the Patriots 13-yard line. Chicago then drove to the 3-yard line, but had to settle for another field goal from Butler after rookie defensive lineman ___E:William "Refrigerator" Perry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Perry_(football))___ was tackled for a 1-yard loss while trying to throw his first NFL pass on a ___E:halfback option play U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halfback_option_play)___ .

On the Patriots' ensuing drive, Dent forced running back ___E:Craig James U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Craig_James_(running_back))___ to fumble, which was recovered by linebacker ___E:Mike Singletary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Singletary)___ at the 13-yard line. Two plays later, Bears fullback ___E:Matt Suhey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Suhey)___ scored on an 11-yard touchdown run to increase the lead to 13–3.
New England took the ensuing kickoff and ran one play before the first quarter ended, which resulted in positive yardage for the first time in the game (a 3-yard run by James).

But after an incomplete pass and a 4-yard loss, they had to send in punter ___E:Rich Camarillo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rich_Camarillo)___ again, and receiver ___E:Keith Ortego U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Ortego)___ returned the ball 12 yards to the 41-yard line. The Bears subsequently drove 59 yards in 10 plays, featuring a 24-yard reception by Suhey, to score on McMahon's 2-yard touchdown run to increase their lead, 20–3. After the ensuing kickoff, New England lost 13 yards in 3 plays and had to punt again, but got the ball back with great field position when defensive back ___E:Raymond Clayborn U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raymond_Clayborn)___ recovered a fumble from Suhey at their own 46-yard line. Patriots coach ___E:Raymond Berry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raymond_Berry)___ then replaced Eason with ___E:Steve Grogan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Grogan)___ to see if he could spark the Patriots offense.
But Grogan could only lead them to the 37-yard line and they decided to punt rather than risk a 55-yard field goal attempt.

The Bears then marched 72 yards in 11 plays, moving the ball inside the Patriots 10-yard line. New England kept them out of the end zone, but Butler kicked his third field goal on the last play of the half to give Chicago a 23–3 halftime lead.

The Bears had absolutely dominated New England in the first half, holding them to 21 offensive plays (only 4 of which resulted in positive yardage), −19 total offensive yards, 2 pass completions, 1 first down, and 3 points.
Meanwhile, Chicago gained 236 yards and scored 23 points themselves.
After the Patriots received the second-half opening kickoff, they managed to get one first down, but then had to punt after Grogan was sacked twice.

Camarillo, who punted 4 times in the first half, managed to pin the Bears back at their own 4-yard line with a Super Bowl record 62-yard punt. But the Patriots defense still had no ability to stop Chicago's offense.
On their very first play, McMahon faked a handoff to Payton, then threw a 60-yard completion to Gault.

Eight plays later, McMahon finished the Super Bowl record 96-yard drive with a 1-yard touchdown run to make the Bears lead 30–3. On New England's second drive of the period, Chicago cornerback Reggie Phillips intercepted a pass from Grogan and returned it 28 yards for a touchdown to increase the lead to 37–3.

On the second play of their ensuing possession, the Patriots turned the ball over again, when receiver ___E:Cedric Jones U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cedric_Jones_(wide_receiver))___ lost a fumble after catching a 19-yard pass from Grogan.

A few plays later, McMahon's 27-yard completion to receiver ___E:Dennis Gentry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dennis_Gentry)___ moved the ball to the 1-yard line, setting up perhaps the most memorable moment of the game. William "the Refrigerator" Perry was brought on to score on offense, as he had done twice in the regular season.
His touchdown made the score 44–3.

The Patriots finally scored a touchdown early in the fourth quarter, advancing the ball 76 yards in 12 plays and scoring on an 8-yard pass from Grogan to receiver ___E:Irving Fryar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irving_Fryar)___ .

But the Bears defense dominated New England for the rest of the game, forcing another fumble, another interception, and defensive lineman ___E:Henry Waechter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Waechter)___ 's sack on Grogan in the end zone for a ___E:safety U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safety_(American_football_score))___ to make the final score 46–10.

One oddity in the Bears victory was that Payton had a relatively poor performance statistically running the ball and never scored a touchdown in Super Bowl XX, his first and only Super Bowl appearance in a Hall of Fame career.

However, if one views the game and watches the Patriots' defense, it is clear that their primary goal was stopping Payton and he frequently had three and four defenders keyed on him on nearly every play. This allowed the rest of the Bears' offense far more opportunities to score than had the Patriots employed a more balanced defense.
Ultimately Payton was the Bears' leading rusher during the game, but the Patriots defense held him to only 61 yards on 22 carries, with his longest run being only 7 yards.

He was given several opportunities to score near the goal line, but New England stopped him every time before he reached the end zone (such as his 2-yard loss from the New England 3-yard line a few plays before Butler's second field goal, and his 2-yard run from the 4-yard line right before McMahon's first rushing touchdown).
Thus, Chicago head coach ___E:Mike Ditka U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Ditka)___ opted to go for other plays to counter the Patriots defense.
Perry's touchdown and McMahon's rushing touchdowns are widely considered as scoring opportunities that were denied to Payton.
Ditka has since gone on record stating that his biggest regret of his career was not creating a scoring opportunity for Payton during the game.
McMahon, who completed 12 out of 20 passes for 256 yards, became the first quarterback in a Super Bowl to score 2 rushing touchdowns.
Bears receiver ___E:Willie Gault U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Gault)___ finished the game with 129 receiving yards on just 4 receptions, an average of over 32.2 yards per catch.
He also returned 4 kickoffs for 49 yards.
Suhey had 11 carries for 52 yards and a touchdown, and caught a pass for 24 yards.
Singletary tied a Super Bowl record with 2 fumble recoveries.
Eason became the first Super Bowl starting quarterback to fail to complete a pass, going 0 for 6 attempts.
The Bears also dominated Patriots starting running back James, holding him to 1 yard on 5 carries, with 1 fumble.
Grogan completed 17 out of 30 passes for 177 yards and 1 touchdown, with 2 interceptions.

Although Fullback ___E:Tony Collins U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Collins_(American_football))___ was the Patriots leading rusher, he was limited to just 4 yards on 3 carries, and caught 2 passes for 19 yards.
New England receiver ___E:Stephen Starring U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Starring)___ returned 7 kickoffs for 153 yards and caught 2 passes for 39 yards.

The Bears were first in scoring defense, allowing only 198 points in the regular season with an average of allowing only 12.4 points/game, as well as scoring more points than given up.  The 198 points allowed were 65 less than the second-most allowed that year, while the point differential of plus-258 is 110 more than the second-ranked differential and the third-highest in NFL history.
They were also second in scoring with 456 points (28.5 points/game), trailing only the ___E:Chargers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_San_Diego_Chargers_season)___ that season.

The Bears' iconic ___E:46 defense U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/46_defense)___ (named after the jersey number of former Bears' safety, ___E:Doug Plank U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doug_Plank)___ ), led by mercurial defensive coordinator ___E:Buddy Ryan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddy_Ryan)___ , was an "attack from all angles" scheme that resulted in, arguably, one of the greatest overall team defenses in league history.
